title: Death by Laser?
caption: Laser guide stars and the Carina Nebula over the Very Large Telescope, Paranal Observatory, Chile
celestial: Photograph taken at Paranal Observatory, Chile

recognition.text: ESO Picture of the Week (an editorial selection, not an audience score).

story: Huge orange beams of light shoot into the sky, looking at first like some fearsome weapon. The reality is far more peaceful, a mix of gas, dust and powerful lasers above ESO's Paranal Observatory in Chile, home of the Very Large Telescope (VLT). The Carina Nebula shows as a pink cloud in the clear sky.

The Carina Nebula is one of the largest nebulae in the southern night sky and an ideal target for the VLT. It is an enormous cloud of dust and gas, and stars inside it ionize the gas and make it glow.

The lasers belong to the Adaptive Optics Facility on one of the VLT's 8.2-meter Unit Telescopes, seen here in full operation. The beams excite sodium particles high in the atmosphere, which then glow, forming artificial stars. By watching these, the telescope can measure how Earth's atmosphere blurs its view and correct for it.

understand.summary: This is a ground-based landscape photograph credited to ESO/G. Hüdepohl. The source does not publish camera, exposure or color-processing details.
understand.eye: A camera gathering light over time may show the nebula's pink glow and the laser beams more strongly than the eye would see them.
